item.title: Keep Her Centred in Portrait

turns.text: Make this landscape clip vertical, 9:16. Keep her centred throughout and keep the full 10 seconds with the original sound. No captions.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing of existing footage while preserving the speaker, duration and source audio.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4 and keep the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Framing style: Crop to fill the frame without stretching; keep her face and head comfortably visible.
answer_sheet.Audio and text: Keep the original speech and sound. No captions or other added text.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 video using the attached woman's actual footage, not a newly generated recreation.
The woman remains horizontally centred with her face and head comfortably visible throughout.
The picture fills the portrait frame without stretching or black bars.
The full 10-second sequence and original speech are retained in sync.
No captions or other text have been added.

turns.text: Make this landscape clip vertical, 9:16. Keep her centred throughout and keep the full 10 seconds with the original sound. No captions. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
For this edit, the cheapest option is a **non-AI 9:16 crop with subject tracking: $0 in Magic Hour credits**. It can keep her centred, preserve all 10 seconds and the original audio, and add no captions.

**I haven’t started anything or spent any credits.** The connected Magic Hour tools don’t expose a straightforward crop/reframe operation with subject tracking and guaranteed original-audio preservation. Using generative video editing instead would cost credits and could alter the footage—so I wouldn’t use it for this request. I also can’t verify an exact generation quote with the tools available here.

Your options:
- **Best fit:** Use a free editor’s crop/position keyframes to follow her. Keep the original audio track untouched and export the full 10 seconds.
- **Smaller:** Export at **480 × 854** (approximately 9:16). This reduces file size, not duration.
- **Shorter:** Would reduce file size and potentially generation cost, but would break your full-10-second requirement.
- **No cropping:** Fit the landscape clip inside a vertical canvas with padding; this preserves the whole frame but makes her smaller.

For a free editor, set the canvas to **9:16**, enlarge the clip to fill it, and keyframe its horizontal position as she moves. That’s the route I recommend rather than spending your credits.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option uses **0 Magic Hour credits**, but I can’t perform that non-AI crop with the connected tools. Sorry—I should have made that limitation clearer. **Nothing has run or been charged.**

To do it free in a video editor:
1. Set the canvas to **9:16** and scale the clip to fill it.
2. Add position keyframes to keep her centred as she moves.
3. Keep the full **10 seconds** and the original audio; add no captions.
4. Export at **720 × 1280**, or **360 × 640** for a smaller file.

Tell me which editor you use, and I’ll give you the exact steps.
